articleBlocks: I first thought the puzzle might be about big count facts, but the clues needed one exact number.
A byte has eight bits, which gives the board a strong first number to test.
Planets in our solar system points to the current count of eight planets.
Legs on a spider made the pattern hard to ignore because spiders have eight legs.
Corners of a cube then confirmed the same number: a cube has eight corners.
Sides of most stop signs points the same way because most stop signs are octagons with eight sides.
The turning point was seeing that each clue came from a different area, but every one landed on eight.
The answer, "Things that come in eights," fits because it explains the whole board with one exact number.
That is why the answer is not a loose category like shapes, computers, or astronomy.
When solving future Pinpoint boards, count facts are worth testing when several clues quietly point to the same number.
The solution is strongest after all five clues pass the same eight-check.
Once the number is visible, none of the clues need a forced reading.
solutionNarrative: I first read Bits in a byte and Planets in our solar system as separate facts and drifted toward random count trivia. Bits in a byte gave one number, but the board was not solved until the same number appeared again.
Legs on a spider changed the direction because spiders have eight legs, giving a second clean eight clue.
I then checked the rest: a byte has 8 bits, the solar system has 8 planets, a cube has 8 corners, and most stop signs have 8 sides.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Things that come in eights", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
